item.text: The source adds detail on replay handling, history ownership, and acceptance recovery. It also qualifies two seed claims: a type-2 edge’s owner may be new if its containing diagram existed in the baseline, and treemap reads can fall back to loading a full session. I’ll reflect both in the diagrams.

  "explanation": "The central tree retains the full proposal lifecycle while shrinking from 119 to 79 lines (33.6%) and from 7,992 to 5,338 characters (33.2%). Five peripheral trees expand push ingestion, workflow resources, change derivation, acceptance, and storage. Modular boundaries appear as public services and private machinery; call sequences explain execution; ownership explains histories, promises, receipts and payloads; data dependencies connect captured inputs to computed review results. Authored change.dependsOn relationships are distinguished from computation dependencies.

All details come from the supplied point definition and six embedded source files. Peripheral additions absent from the seed include enabled-check ordering on push replay, workflow map lifetimes, canonical history ownership, four-at-a-time preview loading, bounded caches, and exact hunk-context checks.

Source-grounded corrections: ChangeSessionService.validateReady permits a new or replaced edge source owner when its containing diagram existed in the baseline; it does not require that owner itself to have existed. readTreemaps can fall back to get(), so avoiding full histories and receipts is not unconditional. update can capture hunks when an existing session lacks a DiffTree. Annotation replacement is optional, although any supplied replacement must cover every generated change. Acceptance checks live document content and name, rather than capturedVersion.

The catalog publication implementation, workflow factory, tool implementation and persistence helpers are outside the supplied source. Their internal atomicity, tool permissions and execution guarantees are therefore not expanded beyond the visible calls and checks.
